data.narrative:
Deep Isolation, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Elizabeth Muller and Richard A. Muller, is evaluated against a universe of 11 comparable companies: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, Nano Nuclear Energy, X-Energy, and Oklo. The company has raised $26M to date.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $26M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A progression to the next stage, yielding $52M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B). The median across this peer set is $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $44M to $929M, with a median of $430M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer-median anchors toward the higher end. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the wide peer range—particularly whether the $6.0B Series B valuation and $200M Series A peer are appropriately calibrated to Deep Isolation's technology maturity and market traction—and whether the $26M raised to date reflects institutional conviction or earlier-stage capital structures that may not predict later-stage pricing.
